body:
# the contributor audit: full local convex-body Lorentz neighborhood



The cited exact sector replacement preserves the actual endpoint support halfplanes in addition to cap/section data. The new proof uses this extra fact correctly. Normalizing support forms by their value one at the ray endpoint gives uniform boundedness from the interior ball; all subsequential limits are the unique old edge supports. In a unique sector, the area equation fixes the sum of the two auxiliary coefficients but would not alone fix their positions. The two limiting support inequalities, combined with strictly positive coefficients, force both to be equalities and hence fix the old vertex. In a double sector, the limiting auxiliary lies on the old bridge segment. All coefficients are bounded, so these subsequence statements yield uniform convergence for every allowed replacement choice.

A fixed exposing functional at each old triangle vertex has a positive gap on the other vertices and all bridge segments. It therefore makes each nearby unique auxiliary an actual exposed vertex. Their inner triangle contains the source. Every other construction point lies uniformly away from the endpoints of its assigned edge. The two-negative-barycentric-coordinate exclusion is valid: a negative i coordinate requires -delta times its own group weight to beat at least c times the other group weight, and the two required strict inequalities contradict delta<c. Nonnegative contributions of the remaining group and triangle vertices may indeed be dropped.

This gives three disjoint outer ears. Clipping a convex hull by an edge line introduces only points on that edge segment, so each ear is the hull of the segment and its assigned exterior vertices. Its roof is concave, piecewise linear, zero at the endpoints and has all nontrivial knots in one compact interior subinterval. The height, area and Lipschitz estimates are uniform. For precision, the vector w should be stated as an outward signed ninety-degree rotation of B-A divided by |B-A|^2; it is not the unit normal divided by that quantity. With that convention the Jacobian is exactly one, as used throughout.

The actual cap indicator differs from the base-step indicator only in a strip of width O(H_e), so its area error is O(H_e^2). The section endpoint equation is a contraction in increments with constant below one-half. This proves a unique crossing and the O(H_e^2) section error without differentiability at any roof knot. The opposite-vertex cap remains uniformly absent. Different edge extensions of a source chord are disjoint, so their lengths add.

The area lower bound E_e>=H_e/2 makes these errors O(delta_0 E), rather than an uncontrolled absolute second-order error. The data increment is O(E); bounded second derivatives of the row functional and E<=3delta_0 control the Taylor remainder by the same relative error. The positive tent decomposition has exactly the printed coefficients and total coefficient 2E_e. All tent peaks stay in the compact interior interval, where the previously proved negative ear derivatives have a common strictly negative bound, continuous in the nearby triangle. This yields the strict linear area decrease with no unproved limit interchange.

If there are no ears, the replacement is its inner triangle. Each actual retained ray support must then equal the unique edge support of that triangle. Thus the original body is contained in the same triangle and has equal area, forcing equality. This validates strictness for every original nontriangle, even when the original boundary is curved. Initially strict rows persist by the source-centered support inclusions and data continuity.

The theorem is a full Hausdorff neighborhood for every fixed strict-incidence triangle, and treats arbitrary convex bodies in that neighborhood. It supplies neither a uniform neighborhood across degenerate triangles nor a global row inequality. The replacement preserves ordinary data and supports, but no compatibility between different mixed fibers has been asserted. Full OC remains unproved.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
